page: Vultr vc2-8c-32gb is a General Purpose virtual machine from the Cloud Compute family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor with 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 640 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate moderate multi-core capabilities alongside weaker single-core execution. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10% at 800.09, whereas the multi-core score reaches an average tier of 6282.15. Memory read bandwidth is average, measuring 516.53 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 40.26 GB/sec for large blocks, though large block write bandwidth drops to a poor 14.02 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks show mixed results, with a weak Passmark CPU encryption score of 2192.65 and a poor single-threaded gzip compression speed of 15.6 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation, this server offers a cost-effective option for workloads requiring substantial memory and storage capacity without demanding sustained, high-performance single-core compute. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, moderate web serving, Redis key-value stores, and general-purpose utility tasks. However, it is less optimal for intensive database operations, heavy cryptography, or large-scale LLM inference due to its shared CPU architecture and lower single-core performance.
